sections.title: STARDUST TO HUMAN
sections.narration: Put your hand on your chest. The iron in your blood, the calcium in your bones, the gold in your ring, none of it was born on Earth. It was forged at a hundred million degrees inside the heart of a star that exploded before the sun even existed. Literally, you are the ashes of a stellar explosion, and the rock beneath your feet? 4 .5 billion years ago it was a boiling inferno at 1200 degrees Celsius. No water, no air, meteorites hammered it every day. So how, did that hell become the place where you are sitting scrolling through your phone? This is the whole story.

sections.title: FROM NOTHING
sections.narration: To tell the story of Earth we have to begin before Earth, before time itself. 13 .8 billion years ago everything was packed into a point smaller than an atom. Then it expanded. The Big Bang, not an explosion like fireworks but space itself swelling faster than light. Three minutes later the first protons appeared, 380 ,000 years later there was light. 200 million years later hydrogen gas gathered grew hotter and lit up. The first star switched on. Inside every star is a furnace, burning hydrogen into carbon, oxygen and eventually iron. The very carbon in your skin, the oxygen you are breathing, the bigger a star the sooner it dies, it collapses inward then explodes. A supernova? As bright as an entire galaxy, scattering gold, silver and uranium across the universe. The gold in a wedding ring was not born on Earth, it was born when two stellar corpses collided.

sections.title: THE SUN CAME FIRST
sections.narration: Fast forward to 4 .6 billion years ago, a cold cloud of stardust millions of times larger than the solar system was drifting through space. Then a nearby star exploded. Its shock wave arrived like an invisible hand crushing the cloud. The cloud collapsed inward, spinning like a whirlpool. At its center the temperature reached 10 million degrees, and it lit up. The newborn sun. The first light in our solar system. There was no Earth yet, just a young sun in the middle surrounded by an enormous wildly spinning disk of dust. That disk was the construction site. Remember this, the sun came first. Earth was the child built from the leftover dust.

sections.title: HELL AND THE MOON
sections.narration: Inside that disk dust grains collided and stuck together. Dust became pebbles, pebbles became house -sized rocks, rocks became planetary embryos. Colliding and merging for 50 million years. The result? A glowing ball of hot rock. The newborn Earth 4 .54 billion years ago, this was hell. The surface was boiling magma at 1200 degrees Celsius. No water. No soil, a sky full of poisonous gases. Thousands of meteorites rained down every day. Then came the apocalypse. A Mars -sized planet called Theia hurtled toward Earth at 40 ,000 kilometers per hour and struck it head on. The impact shattered Theia and blasted Earth's outer layers into space. It looked like the end. But the debris did not escape. Gravity held it nearby. The fragments orbited, collided, stuck together. And in just a hundred years became the moon. The moon is a piece of Earth. Every time you gaze at it you are looking at the scar of the most terrifying accident in our planet's history.

sections.title: WATER FROM THE SKY
sections.narration: After the impact, Earth was a ball of fire. But it had two rescuers, the perfect distance from the sun and just enough size to hold on to water. Earth cooled. Magma hardened into a rocky crust. Volcanoes erupted furiously releasing water vapor and building the first atmosphere. The vapor rose into clouds. Then came rain, rain that lasted, not a few days but thousands of years. Millions of icy comets crashed down bringing even more water. Water filled every low place. Magma basins became oceans. The Red Inferno became a blue planet. The evidence is in Australia. Zircon crystals 4 .4 billion years old formed in the presence of water. Just 150 million years after its birth, Earth already had seas. This was the first great turning point. With water, everything became possible. 3 .8

sections.title: SLIME REWRITES THE SKY
sections.narration: billion years ago on the ocean floor, underwater volcanoes vented hot water rich in chemicals. A tiny fatty membrane folded around itself trapped chemicals inside and learned to copy itself. The first life, just bacteria, for a billion years Earth had nothing but these little things, blue water, green, slimy rocks. Then one branch learned a magic trick, photosynthesis, taking in carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen. Back then, oxygen was poison. It killed almost all the older life. This was the first pollution crisis. The Great Oxidation Event 2 .4 billion years ago. But that same oxygen created the ozone layer, made the sky blue and allowed energy -hungry life to evolve later. The tiniest creatures rewrote the entire sky.

sections.title: FROZEN THEN ALIVE
sections.narration: Cells with nuclei appeared, then multicellular organisms, then sexual reproduction. And Earth nearly died a second time. 720 million years ago it froze into a completely white snowball, ice a kilometer thick. Minus 50 degrees Celsius, but volcanoes under the ice kept erupting. Carbon dioxide built up creating a powerful greenhouse effect that melted the ice. Meltwater carried minerals into the sea, a buffet for life. Then came the Cambrian Explosion 541 million years ago. In 20 million years, eyes appeared. Jointed legs, claws, hard shells, the ocean went from a stagnant pond to an arena of monsters. 470

sections.title: LAND AND THE GREAT DYING
sections.narration: million years ago the first plants crept onto land, barely as tall as a finger. 390 million years later they had become enormous forests. Lobe -finned fish crawled ashore and became four -legged animals, your walking ancestors. 300 million years ago the continents joined into the supercontinent Pangea. Then came the greatest catastrophe. 252 million years ago volcanoes in Siberia erupted for a million years. Lava covered 7 million square kilometers, the ocean turned sour as vinegar. Temperatures rose by 10 degrees. 90 % of marine species and 70 % of land species vanished. The Permian Mass extinction. It looked like a complete reset, but the 10 % that survived became an opportunity.

sections.title: THE DINOSAURS LAST DAY
sections.narration: After the extinction, one branch of reptiles rose to power, the dinosaurs. They appeared 230 million years ago, growing into giants like the 9 -ton Tyrannosaurus They ruled for 165 million years. Mammals were just little mouse -like creatures hiding in the night. 66 million years ago a rock 10 kilometers wide raced toward Earth at 70 ,000 kilometers per hour. 20 times the speed of a bullet. It struck Mexico, the energy of 10 billion atomic bombs. A tsunami a kilometer high, hot rocks fell like a rain of fire burning every forest. Dust hid the earth. So to synthesize, herbivores died, carnivores followed, 75 % of life vanished. The weakest creatures survived, tiny mammals that could dig burrows, eat almost anything and keep themselves warm. Our ancestors?

sections.title: THE FINAL SECOND
sections.narration: The forests returned. With the dinosaurs gone, mammals grew larger, mammoths, 30 -meter whales, primates. Seven million years ago one branch of apes came down to ground and walked on two legs. Three million years ago they learned to strike stones into knives. 300 ,000 years ago homo sapiens appeared, If we compress 4 .54 billion years into one year, Earth forms on January 1. Life around 3 .8 billion years ago falls in early March. Dinosaurs arrive around December 13. The asteroid strikes on December 26. Homo sapiens arrives around 11 .25 pm on December 31. 5 ,000 years of written history including dynasties, wars and phones fit into roughly the final 35 seconds. Earth has been magma, it has frozen solid, it has been smashed apart and still healed, it does not need us, we need it. Because after 4 .5 billion years of chaos it has finally become peaceful enough for a species that can tell stories. For you, to sit here and hear the story yourself, you are made of stardust. Do not live like a speck of dust.
